subject: Operational boundary & tenant egress — annotated Q&A for SOC 2
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@vectorhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 evidence: network-level architecture for Private deployment

Hi Diego,

We're working through VectorHealth's SOC 2 scoping and the auditor is asking for a consolidated network-level architecture that explains tenant isolation for Private deployments. Specifically we need:
- A diagram that shows control-plane vs data-plane boundaries for Private (VPC) deployments, including where KMS/HSM keys live and who controls them.
- A short narrative (one page) describing tenant egress controls (NAT, egress proxies, allowlists) and how we prevent cross-tenant data leakage.
- A mapping of those elements to SIG/CAIQ controls (network segmentation, key management, audit logs).

Can you share an annotated diagram (PDF) and any matrices you already have? We're hoping to include them in our auditor packet by next Wednesday (2025-10-07). If anything needs to be redacted for IP reasons, flag it and we'll handle secure transmission.

Best,
Alice Park
Senior Security Engineer, VectorHealth

---
VectorHealth SOC2 Team <soc2@vectorhealth.com>
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@vectorhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence: network-level architecture for Private deployment

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (security architecture) and Marissa (evidence packaging) to assemble a concise packet. Quick notes so we're aligned before we export diagrams: 

1) Diagram level: we can provide two artifacts — (A) an annotated topology PDF that highlights control/data plane split, tenancy overlay, and KMS ownership; and (B) an evidence matrix (CSV) that maps the components to SIG/CAIQ controls.
2) Redaction: we have a standard redaction template for internal service names. We'll mark anything proprietary; if VectorHealth needs full internal names for the auditor we can arrange an NDA-backed bundle.
3) Custody and access: keys for customer-owned Private deployments are optionally customer-managed (KMS in customer VPC) or Redwood-managed in a tenant-dedicated KMS partition. We'll indicate the pattern used in your account as a footnote.
4) Egress controls: our Private deployment pattern supports either:
   - Managed NAT + egress proxies with per-tenant allowlists (recommended), or
   - Controlled egress through customer-managed transit gateways for fully air-gapped scenarios.

Marissa/Kimberly — can you confirm the most current annotated topology file and whether we should include flow logs and retention proofs in this packet? Also tagging that the auditor will want evidence of log forwarding and retention windows.

If we can get a quick list of any additional redaction constraints from Alice today, we can aim to deliver the PDF + matrix by EOD Tuesday (2025-09-30).

Thanks,
Diego
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-29T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence: network-level architecture for Private deployment

Diego — attaching the latest artifacts (see list below). Short answers inline to Alice's original bullets.

Attachments in our draft packet:
- annotated-topology-v2.pdf (diagram, pages: control-plane layer, data-plane layer, egress paths)
- egress-policy-matrix.csv (per-tenant rules, egress destinations, allowed ports)
- initial-legend.png (diagram legend and traffic classification)

Narrative highlights to include in the one-page summary (copy this into the PDF appendix):
- Control plane vs data plane: control plane components (orchestration, image registry access, model catalog service) are hosted in a customer-dedicated control partition with strict role-based access controls and no direct inbound tenant network access. Data plane hosts inference runtime instances inside the customer VPC with ephemeral interfaces; only outbound connections are allowed to designated telemetry endpoints and customer-configured egress destinations.
- KMS boundaries: for Private deployments we support two modes — customer-managed KMS (recommended for highest assurance) and Redwood-managed tenant-key rings in a partitioned HSM. The diagram shows both flows; the matrix flags which controls apply for each mode.
- Egress filtering and leakage prevention: per-tenant egress proxies apply URL/IP allowlists; we enforce header-stripping and tokenization on outbound telemetry; intra-host file systems are ephemeral and wiped on instance termination.
- Audit logs & retention: VPC flow logs + application-level access logs are forwarded to the customer's logging endpoint (or to a dedicated Redwood retention bucket if customer opts). Retention windows are documented in the matrix (default 90 days, configurable). We will attach sample flow log lines and a screenshot of retention policy as evidence if requested.

Marissa — I recommend including the flow log sample and a signed statement from infra ops about ephemeral volumes; that helps SIG reviewers.

Alice — if you prefer we can replace any internal service label with generic placeholders (SERVICE-A) before sending to the auditor. Confirm and we'll sanitize.

—Kimberly
Principal Security Architect, Redwood Inference
